$description: Component-override tier — a sparse escape-hatch namespace. INTENTIONALLY MINIMAL at this stage; this file exists to establish the convention, not to populate it. A component-override token is added here ONLY when a specific component needs to diverge from the semantic tier and no semantic role fits. Naming convention: mf.component.<component>.<property> (e.g. mf.component.button.destructive-hover), each aliasing a semantic --mf-* role or a raw value. Prefer adding/using a semantic role over an override; overrides are the exception. The example below is commented-out-by-convention (kept under an inert `$example` group so nothing is emitted) purely to document the shape. `mf.component.<component>.radius` is a reserved property name within this convention: mod-core/gui/style-dictionary/build-tokens.mjs (see componentRadiusOverrideBlock) recognizes it specifically and emits a `[data-mf-component="<component>"]` scoped block that shadows --radius-{sm,md,lg,xl} for that component alone (followup 7nrP) — see tokens/CONTRACT.md's "Per-component radius override tier" section for the full contract. Every other `<property>` name in this file is a plain alias with no special build-time handling.

component.$description: Empty by design. Add real per-component override tokens as siblings of $example when a genuine need arises.

$example.$description: Illustrative only — task 002 must NOT emit tokens under $example. Shows the intended mf.component.<component>.<property> shape.

destructive-hover.$description: EXAMPLE ONLY. How a button-specific override would alias a raw or semantic value.

radius.$description: EXAMPLE ONLY. How a component would opt out of the global --mf-radius scale (e.g. pill-shaped buttons) via the reserved `radius` property — see tokens/CONTRACT.md's "Per-component radius override tier" section.
